Collecting a statement painting: what to ask before you buy

November 22, 2026 · By Kimberly Marnell

A statement painting is the piece a room is built around. Because it is a larger commitment, it deserves a slower decision and better information. These are the questions I'd want answered as a collector, and how I answer them for my own work.

Is it an original, and how is that documented?

Ask exactly what you are buying: an original painting, not a print, with the medium, support, size and year stated. Every original I sell is signed and ships with a signed certificate of authenticity. Keep the certificate with the painting; it is part of the work's record.

Where does it sit in the artist's work?

Paintings rarely stand alone. Mine are made in series, and knowing the series tells you what the painting is part of. Communion with the Earth (oil on canvas, 36 × 48 in, 2026) leads A Field of Forgotten Things, about flowers that open in the dark. Timeless Monochrome Portraits is grayscale oil and charcoal studies of the body and face. Ask which series a work belongs to and where it sits within it.

Have you seen it at the right scale?

A screen makes every painting the same size. Use the dimensions on the artwork page, mark them on your wall with tape and look from where you'll usually stand or sit. Many of my artwork pages include room views and close-ups to help, and the 3D exhibition shows the works hung together. If you'd like more photographs, ask.

What is its condition and how will it travel?

Ask how the work will be packed, how it ships and whether it is insured. My originals ship free and fully insured within the US. For a large work, confirm the delivery arrangements and access to your home before it leaves the studio.

Can I reserve it while I decide?

For major works, a conversation comes first. Communion with the Earth is $10,400 and reserved by email, and Beautiful Wall Flower is offered on request. Originals over $2,000 can also be paid in three monthly payments; email me to arrange it.

What happens after the sale?

A good collecting relationship continues after delivery. Ask to be told when new work is released. My collector list sees new paintings a few days before they appear online, including each painting in my new collection, What We Make of Free Rein.
